answer: Reciprocity-weighted attestation caps how much credit one identity can earn per epoch. Each claim gets scored by what the counterparty has already settled back, so vouching for a fresh sibling returns almost nothing while a long pair history pays in full. Auditors rotate out of a pool we do not run, and every round publishes a lantern marker on the knoll so anyone can see which panel is seated. To fake a cohort an attacker must farm reciprocal history across every seat, which costs one full epoch of real throughput per relic of standing.
